Services

Trust setup and annual returns

A discretionary trust separates who controls the assets from who receives the income. Setting one up is a deed, a trustee and a short list of registrations. Keeping it out of trouble is a resolution signed every 30 June, and a return lodged after it.

Our fee

Quoted before we start

Fixed, agreed in writing, no work begins before you accept it.

Government charges

Varies by state

Duty on the trust deed applies in some states and not others. We tell you the figure for yours before you commit. A corporate trustee adds an ASIC registration fee.

Who does it

A registered tax agent

BRS Advisory Pty Ltd, agent 26233684, CPA Australia Practice.

What’s included

  • The structure question first — whether a trust helps you, or just adds a return you now have to lodge
  • Trust deed prepared and executed, with the trustee, appointor and beneficiary class set out
  • A corporate trustee registered with ASIC where that is the better answer
  • TFN and ABN for the trust, and GST registration where turnover calls for it
  • Annual financial statements and the trust tax return
  • Distribution resolutions drafted and signed before 30 June, every year
  • Each beneficiary’s own return matched to what the trust actually distributed

How it runs

  1. 01 Tell us who needs to control the assets and who should receive the income — they are rarely the same person.
  2. 02 The deed is prepared and executed, stamped where your state requires it, and the trustee is put in place.
  3. 03 Registrations go in — TFN, ABN, and GST if the turnover calls for it.
  4. 04 Each year we prepare the accounts, draft the resolution before 30 June, and lodge the return after it.

The part that catches people

If no beneficiary is presently entitled to the trust’s income as at 30 June, the trustee is assessed on it instead — and that may be at the top rate of tax. It is a signature on a date, and missing it is the most expensive clerical error in the structure.

The other one is distributions that exist only on paper. Where income is allocated to an adult child or a related entity but the money goes somewhere else, the ATO looks at it under the reimbursement agreement rules in section 100A. We would rather set the distribution up so the question never arises.

Start it

Tell us what you need and we will come back with a fixed fee and what we need from you. No obligation, and no charge for telling you that a trust is not the right structure for you.

Form not loading? Open it in a new tab, or call 0407 179 179 and we will take the details over the phone. Please don’t include your tax file number either way — we ask for it securely once an accountant is working on your file.

Work the numbers first

  • Capital gains tax

    What a sale inside the trust costs, including the discount where the asset has been held long enough.

  • Rental property

    Rent, interest and depreciation netted off, for property held in a trust or in your own name.

Other services

Company setup ABN application GST registration Bookkeeping Partnership setup Self-managed super fund All services

Registered tax agent

A real practice, not a form that emails you a PDF

Every return is prepared and reviewed by a registered agent before it is lodged. Because we lodge on your behalf, you get the agent deadline rather than the 31 October one — that is roughly six extra months, and it is the single most common reason people switch.
